transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-03-12 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~53m | Recording: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Solutions); Raj (CTO), Anne-Marie (Cloud Architect), Samir (Security), Tara (Platform)

Summary (auto): Customer evaluating Redwood Private deployment. Wants minimal network changes and stable egress. Questions about peering, transit gateway, private endpoints, regional isolation, and KMS.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today. quick round of intros?
[00:10] Raj (Cedarline): Raj here, CTO. we've been kicking around LLM infra for a bit, use-cases are document summarization and risk-classification; must stay in EU.
[00:18] Anne-Marie: Anne-Marie, Cloud Architect, I own networking for the platform.
[00:21] Samir: Samir, Security — I'll be driving compliance checks.
[00:25] Tara: Tara, Platform Eng. I'll likely own any peering/config changes.
[00:28] Maya: Great. from Redwood side Liam will cover the technical routing bits and Priya can help with the onboarding flow. quick context question: are you currently running anything through AWS Transit Gateway or mostly VPC peering?
[00:40] Anne-Marie: We run TGW for cross-account routing across our EU accounts, yes. we also have some direct peering for low-latency services.
[00:47] Liam (Redwood SE): got it. that maps well to the options we usually see — we support both peering + privatelink style endpoints and TGW attachments. If you prefer not to create new cross-account peering, we can attach to TGW.
[00:58] (noise)
[01:05] Raj: Our blocker is egress IP stability. Compliance wants a small set of IPs we can allowlist, and any scaling shouldn't change them frequently.
[01:13] Priya: we have pub/sub on that. For dedicated private deployments we can provide static egress IPs in many cases, or work with a NAT gateway in your VPC. question: do you have a fixed set of external endpoints that need to talk out, or are you just webhooks?
[01:28] Tara: mostly internal calls to our data lake, but also some SaaS callbacks to a small set of partners. we need stable egress because our partners do allow-lists.
[01:35] Liam: two patterns: 1) Redwood sits in your VPC and uses your NAT/GW — that keeps egress IPs under your control; 2) Redwood-hosted private dataplane with a small set of our egress IPs — we can set up stable IP ranges but that is more common for Dedicated vs hosted. note: our private model lets you pin to a region so egress residency is controllable.
[01:50] Anne-Marie: Tell me more about the private endpoints approach. we prefer not to have to manage long-lived peering in many accounts.
[01:56] Liam: we can offer endpoint-style setup (similar to AWS PrivateLink) where you create an interface endpoint in your VPC that points to our private service. That is least intrusive — your traffic never leaves the AWS backbone. Downsides: endpoint ENIs per AZ and costs, and you still need route table/NACL considerations.
[02:15] Raj: How does that affect latency? we are sensitive on inference latency for chat use-cases.
[02:20] Liam: PrivateLink usually adds a small hop but generally under 2–5ms in-region. bigger factors are model size and KV cache locality; if you put the service in the same region and use our dedicated capacity we can get to consistent single-digit ms per token for smaller models.
[02:34] Samir: KMS — we need to bring our own key for any customer data crossing boundaries. does Redwood integrate with external KMS/HSM?
[02:39] Priya: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and HSM in Private deployments. there are some handshake steps for key rotation and audit & we log key usage in audit trails.
[02:50] Anne-Marie: Are audit logs exportable to our SIEM? we need to keep extended retention for 13 months.
[02:55] Priya: yes we can stream audit logs to your CloudWatch/Storage using an on-prem connector or an event export. retention is configurable in the Private console; we usually recommend shipping a copy to customer S3 for long-term retention.
[03:10] Tara: region gating — we want inference to run only in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. is that supported?
[03:15] Liam: absolutely. our Private control plane can be configured to only allow model serving in specific regions, and we support region pinning per-tenant. note: if you require active-active across two regions you'll need cross-region peering or TGW attachments for KV cache replication.
[03:30] Raj: Replication — will Redis/KV be in our account or in Redwood's infra?
[03:34] Liam: two options: host KV in your VPC (best for data control) or use our managed KV with encryption-at-rest and customer KMS. hosting KV yourself requires us to configure network access and IAM roles for the service.
[03:47] Anne-Marie: If we host KV, what ports/protocols? we run TLS over TCP, standard ports.
[03:52] Liam: TLS on 443 is supported for the control plane and data plane handshakes; for internal high-throughput KV we use gRPC over TLS — typically blocked to a small set of IPs. we'll provide a narrow CIDR set.
[04:03] (transcription note: "g r p c" sometimes transcribed as "grpc")
[04:10] Samir: any SOC2 / ISO artifacts? we need to pre-screen before we hand off secrets to a vendor.
[04:15] Maya: we'll share our SOC2 Type II report and our security whitepaper. action: I'll attach those in the follow-up.
[04:22] Tara: lateral question: do you need changes in our route tables for TF-managed infra? we prefer infra-as-code.
[04:27] Priya: we can provide TF modules and sample CloudFormation snippets. customers often drop them into their infra repo and tweak.
[04:34] Raj: licensing/contract: if we go Private, what's the lead time to get an environment up?
[04:39] Maya: typical onboarding for Private, including network setup and KMS, is 3–6 weeks depending on approvals and cross-account peering or TGW attachments. Dedicated reserved capacity is a bit faster if network is already in place.
[04:51] Anne-Marie: for TGW attachment, will we need to share route tables with Redwood?
[04:56] Liam: you don't share route tables, you create a TGW attachment and we program routes into our side. in cross-account TGW you can restrict which route tables are used. there's an IAM-level trust and we do a limited set of API calls; we'll run through the exact permissions in the playbook.
[05:12] Raj: what about IP exhaustion / subnet sizing? we like to avoid touching prod subnets.
[05:17] Liam: typically we recommend isolating private endpoints and compute in dedicated subnets per environment (prod/staging). small /26 or /24 ranges work depending on scale — our playbook will include sizing guidance by expected TCP connections and concurrent sessions.
[05:30] Anne-Marie: cost tradeoffs: endpoints vs peering vs TGW?
[05:34] Maya: endpoints: lower infra change, higher per-ENI cost; peering: cheap, but cross-account peering management overhead; TGW: best for multi-account scale and centralized routing, more configuration up-front. we'll include an expected cost comparison matrix in the follow-up doc.
[05:52] Tara: do you have examples of customers with strict EU-only residency? we want references or a short case study.
[05:56] Maya: yes, we can share a redacted case study and architecture diagram.
[06:00] (pause)
[06:10] Anne-Marie: our security team also wants assurance about ephemeral keys and session behavior. if a token is compromised what's the blast radius?
[06:18] Priya: tokens are short-lived and tied to the service account. for Private deployments you can require mutual TLS and we support certificate rotation. we also support session-level audit so you can see which calls used which keys.
[06:33] Raj: one more: can Redwood do a blackbox latency benchmark against our network? we'd like a simple ping/throughput test to validate region placement and egress path.
[06:41] Liam: yes — we can run a 1–2 day bench with a small script that hits a test endpoint in your account or in an isolated test VPC. we'll coordinate IPs and firewall rules.
[06:53] Samir: procurement / contract question: do you do SOC2 + local DPA for EU?
[06:58] Maya: yes we have a DPA that accommodates EU regulations; legal will be looped in after initial POI.
[07:05] Tara: timeline — we want to decide vendor by end of Q2 2026. if Redwood can demo a running private environment with our peering pattern that'd accelerate.
[07:12] Maya: understood. we'll prioritize the transit design deep-dive and the connectivity checklist.
[07:20] (cross talk)
[07:30] Liam: a few clarifying tech questions for your infra team: 1) do you have active NAT gateways per account or centralized egress? 2) are you using AWS PrivateLink today for other vendors? 3) approximate concurrency for inference (requests/sec)?
[07:45] Anne-Marie: NATs are per-account for prod, centralized for shared services. we use PrivateLink for a couple of SaaS partners. concurrency: around 60–150 rps for burst windows.
[07:56] Liam: great — that helps us size. for 150 rps with medium models we would recommend dedicated reserved capacity or autoscaling Dedicated with predictable pooling to keep token latency down.
[08:10] Raj: any gotchas on DNS? we use split-horizon DNS and have private hosted zones. will PrivateLink resolvers handle that?
[08:17] Priya: yes, we provide instructions for private zone entries and for endpoint DNS names. sometimes customers handle it via Route53 private zones and alias records. we'll include a DNS playbook.
[08:32] Tara: do you support SAML SSO for admin console? we want RBAC mapped to our IdPs.
[08:36] Maya: yes SSO via SAML/OIDC and SCIM provisioning are supported; RBAC roles can be synced to your groups.
[08:44] (background typing)
[08:55] Maya: ok wrapping — recap of next steps: Maya to send checklist and SOC2, Liam to prepare transit diagram + bench plan, Anne-Marie to share CIDRs and NAT details. schedule week of 3/16 for a technical deep-dive.
[09:14] Raj: sounds good, appreciate it.
[09:20] Maya: thanks everyone; we'll follow up with calendar invites and a short pack.

(Transcript ends — rough timings; some words may be mis-transcribed, esp. acronyms and product names.)

Automated action items (extracted): see action_items above.

Notes: customer extremely constrained on region (EU only) and allowlist IPs. prefer Private deployment ideally in their VPC with KMS BYOK and audit log export. follow-up materials promised: connectivity checklist, SOC2, TF module samples, TGW peering diagram, latency bench plan.
